The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Set β0 = β/2. There is b∗ > 0, depending only on the fixed bounds in Proposition 2.9, for which the following holds. Suppose b ≤ b∗, K(ε) → ∞, and J(ε) → ∞ is a fixed power of 1 + | log ε|. Then rε u,t = f(t) − Gε,J,K u,t , sup 0≤u≤t≤T t−u≤b ∥rε u,t∥Bol,β0 =: ηε −→ 0. (4.10) All the reference sums and residuals have uniformly bounded norms at this one fixed exponent. The proof uses only short-layer tree summability and two-body scattering.
